summary: Brick light on Battery Weed at the Narrows, lit in 1903 to replace the Fort Tompkins light; discontinued in 1965 and relit by volunteers in 2005.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends says the light was discontinued in 1965 when the Verrazano-Narrows Bridge opened, and relit in 2005; the USLHS record gives 'Year Discontinued: 1965-2005' and an active aid. Dark for those forty years, then relit. Wikipedia (not cited) says the same.

LighthouseFriends lists William B. Davis, Jr. as head keeper of the Fort Tompkins light from 1870 to 1903; the USLHS roster begins his Fort Wadsworth stint in 1903. Both place him at the station that succeeded Fort Tompkins; the roster lists only this station's years.

notes_for_editor: (1) Keepers: the roster (USLHS) has 37 lines from 1903; each line carries its USLHS person slug. The LighthouseFriends keeper list also names the Fort Tompkins heads from 1828 (Benjamin Church onward); those belong to us-ny-fort-tompkins and are not on this roster. (2) Staffing and the 1958 quarrel: LighthouseFriends reports a fatal 1958 quarrel between two Coast Guard keepers, Somogyi and Hughes, and a 1959 acquittal. Omitted from the story as a private matter not about the light; their roster lines remain, as the archive prints them. The editor may decide. (3) LighthouseFriends also reports the 1902 death of Alfred Carlow at Fort Tompkins, keeper of Old Orchard Shoal at the time: omitted, personal, and not this light's history. (4) Light status: USLHS records 'Year Discontinued: 1965-2005' and 'Active Aid to Navigation?: Yes'; LighthouseFriends says relit 2005 (solar). The Light List (navcen) was not opened (HTTP 403), so the current characteristic is unverified and the record's 'sources differ' note is not resolved by the Light List. (5) Lens: the USLHS record says the current optic is removed; no present optic is described in the sources read. (6) Height: USLHS gives 15 ft base-to-lantern and 75 ft focal height; the record's 4.6 m and 23.0 m match. (7) Lighthouse Board FY1894 fog-signal passage is garbled by OCR and not quoted; the FY1899 and FY1900 text is used. (8) The 1915 Bulletin OCR garbles 'Fort Wadsworth' ('Vadsworth'); quotes avoid the name. (9) 'Bonee (1970-)' is printed by the roster with no surname. (10) Joe Esposito is named as LighthouseFriends names him (public role, 2002-2005 restoration). The Preservation League newsletter cited by LighthouseFriends was not read; a Lighthouse Digest 100th-anniversary story returned HTTP 404. (11) Chronicling America searches for Fort Wadsworth and light (1902-1905) returned no usable station reports; not exhaustive. (12) The NPS Battery Weed page was not read. (13) Wikipedia's claim that the lantern was possibly moved from Fort Tompkins is not used; LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Board say the Fort Tompkins building became the keeper's dwelling. (13) Light-House Board volumes (FY1899, FY1900, FY1901): printed page numbers were not readable in the corpus (it gives scan pages only), so the story and sources cite 'scan p.' N. The FY1900 text itself prints the Board's 1892 report as 'page 68', which is what the story cites for the 1892 statement. (14) The 'Appleton tract' passage was read in the FY1901 corpus text: the keeper's dwelling site on the north corner of the Appleton tract, ceded in 1898, had been occupied by the War Department and another site was selected. (15) The 'Head: Benjamin Church (1828' LighthouseFriends list begins with the Fort Tompkins keepers; William B. Davis, Jr. (1870 - 1903) is read from that list, which is why the story says LighthouseFriends's list gives him 1870 to 1903. (16) Verification pass 2026-10-28: 'The position was poor' was removed (unsourced); the footnote gaps were filled; feet were given in metres; 'the fort then passed' now says 'the lighthouse', as LighthouseFriends does.
